title: LangChain Python project curriculum
scope: The 60 leaf/menu entries shown in the four supplied screenshots, with current official source links. Group labels are not counted. This is not an inventory of every provider integration or every API in the larger LangChain ecosystem.
collection_type: Paraphrased topic and code-pattern inventory, source links for full documentation examples, and representative original Python recipes. Not a verbatim mirror of the documentation.
recommendation: Three progressively more capable projects sharing infrastructure; start with P1. Cover alternative integrations and UI modes through isolated labs.
recipe_validation: Python syntax parsed with ast; no dependency import, provider request, database operation, or deployment executed.

architecture.frontend: React/TypeScript on Cloudflare; useStream plus AI Elements as the proposed main path.
architecture.backend: Python LangChain agents and LangGraph workflows behind a compatible agent server; local development first, persistent backend host for deployment.
architecture.data: Supabase Postgres for business records, pgvector document retrieval, checkpoints, and long-term memories. Optional Supabase Auth and Storage for user identity and uploads.
architecture.llm: OpenAI integration; model identifier selected through OPENAI_MODEL after capability/access verification.
architecture.protocol: Native frontend SDKs need the matching agent-server protocol. Plain FastAPI SSE alone does not supply run, history, resume, queue, or reconnect endpoints.
architecture.memory: Checkpoint state, cross-thread memories, and document embeddings are three separate storage concerns.
architecture.authorization: Verify identity at backend; authorize each thread, run, and data/tool access. Apply RLS on exposed Supabase tables. Direct privileged DB access does not automatically inherit frontend JWT/RLS behavior.
architecture.secrets: Keep model credentials, Postgres URI, and Supabase secret/service credentials server-side.
architecture.missing_setup: Persistent Python backend hosting for a shared deployment, Postgres connection URI/credentials for checkpointers, and a LangSmith account/API key for the Studio/tracing/evaluation lessons.

projects.name: Document knowledge assistant
projects.example_request: Compare our onboarding and refund policies and cite the relevant source sections.
projects.users: A small team querying its internal documents, manuals, and policies.
deliverables: Document ingestion with source/version metadata, parsing, chunking, embeddings, and pgvector retrieval.
Cited answers with explicit insufficient-evidence behavior.
Persistent chat, cross-thread approved preferences, streaming text and progress.
Typed answer cards, branching chat, reference Chat UI, and a Cloudflare frontend.
proposed_acceptance: 30 manually reviewed questions; at least 85% correct and evidence-backed answers as an initial learning target.
Every shown citation resolves to an authorized stored excerpt.
Two-user isolation and backend restart recovery pass.
projects.implementation_structure: One feature per module; minimal package initializer; startup-only main.py; separate application/ingestion coordinators. See document_assistant_modules.json.

projects.name: Customer support and order workflow
projects.example_request: Investigate order DEMO-42, prepare a resolution, and let a reviewer approve the ticket update.
projects.users: Support agents handling orders and customer tickets.
deliverables: Read tools for fictional customers, orders, and policy lookup.
Draft/approve/edit/reject workflow with a durable pause and audit trail.
Triage-to-specialist handoffs, runtime auth context, guardrails, and middleware.
Tool cards, controlled UI, client actions, and sequential message queues.
proposed_acceptance: Unapproved write proposals never reach the write adapter.
Retry or replay of an approved action does not duplicate it.
Role and tenant authorization is checked inside tools.
Review survives restart and handles edit/reject decisions.

projects.name: Business research and operations dashboard
projects.example_request: Explain this month's delivery delays using the uploaded reports and order metrics; produce a cited dashboard.
projects.users: An operations manager reviewing documents and business metrics.
deliverables: Research lead, document specialist, metrics specialist, and synthesis/verification workflow.
Router, subagents, on-demand skills, and a custom graph.
Project-owned MCP read services with connection/auth exercises.
Long-running background reports with rejoin, checkpoint inspection, and replay-safe outputs.
Declarative report UI plus isolated open-ended UI and integration comparison labs.
proposed_acceptance: Every key report claim links to a source or deterministic metric.
Browser refresh rejoins the same retained run.
Generated UI is validated against a catalog or isolated in a sandbox.
Compare specialist quality, time, and tokens against a single-agent baseline.

schedule_assumption: Approximately 10-15 focused hours/week, with basic Python, HTTP, SQL, and React familiarity. Estimates are planning judgments, not documentation guarantees.

phases.focus: Environment, model/messages, one tool, structured output, local agent server and trace.
P1 ingestion, retrieval, citations, memory, streaming, Cloudflare UI, and evaluation baseline.
P2 domain tools, policies, custom middleware, durable approval, handoffs, action idempotency, and UI.
P3 routing, specialist tools, custom graph, skills, MCP, reconnect, and declarative reports.
Remaining integration/UI labs, replay and failure exercises, deployment, evaluation comparison, and documentation.
